title: Model Context Protocol and the “too many tools” problem.
summary: Summary withheld: an Opus review found that the machine-written summary did not match the post. Read the original post.

quotes.text: Having too many tools exposed in an MCP server can degrade the performances and the output of your LLM!
quotes.why_it_matters: Directly states the core problem that motivates the entire discussion about tool management

quotes.text: if tools are crowding out the context window, there's less room for context about the current project or goal.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains the root cause of performance degradation and why limiting tools matters for agent effectiveness

quotes.text: a well-designed MCP server gives agents exactly what they need to accomplish their goals without overwhelming them with choices they don't need.
quotes.why_it_matters: Summarizes the design philosophy and best practice recommendation for building effective MCP servers
